## Purpose and Entry Points
Droidspaces is a privileged, static-musl Linux container runtime for Android, Linux desktops, and minimal Linux environments. It creates namespace-isolated containers capable of running real init systems. The CLI enters through `src/main.c`; core public contracts are in `src/include/droidspace.h`. The Android management app starts at `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/DroidspacesApplication.kt` and `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/MainActivity.kt`.

## Native Runtime and Lifecycle
The C runtime parses configuration and commands, validates host support, then creates, starts, monitors, enters, stops, and reports on named containers. Lifecycle concerns are distributed across `src/container.c`, `src/daemon.c`, and `src/monitor.c`; process/PID tracking is a separate boundary in `src/pid.c`. Runtime setup is designed for direct root execution rather than a dependency on a host container daemon.

## Isolation, Mounts, and Security
Container creation composes Linux PID, mount, UTS, IPC, network, and cgroup namespace behavior, plus filesystem root switching and bind mounts. Principal implementation stages are `src/virtualize.c`, `src/mount.c`, and `src/cgroup.c`. Default hardening applies capability and syscall restrictions through `src/seccomp.c`; hardware exposure and privileged options intentionally relax portions of that model. This is isolation for trusted power-user workloads, not a security boundary for hostile root users.

## Networking and Host Integration
Networking supports host sharing, isolated NAT, no-network, and gateway-oriented modes. The network subsystem configures interfaces, netlink state, DHCP, and firewall/NAT rules through `src/net/network.c`, `src/net/netlink.c`, and `src/net/iptables.c`. Android-specific display, audio, X11, and GPU integration are native runtime extensions in `src/android/x11.c`, `src/android/virgl.c`, and `src/android/pulseaudio.c`.

## Android Bootstrap and Persistence
The Android app packages architecture-specific BusyBox, shell scripts, and a boot module to install/manage the native binary and persistent daemon modes. Material deployment assets are `Android/app/src/main/assets/boot-module/service.sh`, `Android/app/src/main/assets/boot-module/post-fs-data.sh`, and `Android/app/src/main/assets/binaries`. Native-init and service/module integration artifacts live under `init/android-service`; Linux service integration is `init/systemd-service/droidspaces.service`. These bridge Android root/SELinux constraints and let containers outlive the app process.

## Android App Control Plane
The Kotlin Android app is a Compose-based control plane over local root commands and persisted container state, rather than a remote service client. Navigation and workflow screens are rooted at `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/ui/navigation/DroidspacesNavigation.kt`; stateful operations flow through `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/ui/viewmodel/ContainerOperationsViewModel.kt` and `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/ui/viewmodel/ContainerInstallationViewModel.kt`. Native-command construction, execution, installation, rootfs download, and container metadata are handled by `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/util/ContainerCommandBuilder.kt`, `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/util/ContainerOperationExecutor.kt`, and `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/util/ContainerManager.kt`.

## Installation, Rootfs, and Terminal Flows
Container installation obtains/configures a rootfs, optionally manages sparse ext4 images, then invokes runtime boot with persistent configuration. This boundary is represented by `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/util/ContainerInstaller.kt`, `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/util/RootfsDownloadManager.kt`, and `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/util/SparseImageInstaller.kt`. Interactive execution flows from the app’s terminal backend/session service into a container PTY: `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/service/TerminalSessionService.kt`, `Android/app/src/main/java/com/droidspaces/app/ui/terminal/TerminalBackEnd.kt`, and native `src/terminal.c`.

## Build and External Dependencies
The native implementation is C, intended as a statically linked musl binary; build/release orchestration is centered on `Makefile`, with Nix definitions in `flake.nix` and `nix/defaults.nix`. The Android APK is Gradle/Kotlin-based via `Android/app/build.gradle.kts`. External vendored dependencies include BusyBox, socket daemon support, and web assets under `external/busybox`, `external/socketd`, and `external/www`; no network control-plane service is implied by the repository.
